title: The Magi and the Jews
english: …matters. Marvel at the mystery with me and accept the gospels without hesitation. She says: 'Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.' We should learn from the archangelic words of Gabriel about the Lord's birth and follow his paths.

The Magi teach us to be pious, rather let us be instructed; they, searching for the child guided by a star, did not ask those being questioned: 'How is the conception divine? How is the womb without spot? How is the offspring incorruptible? How is the mother in virgins after the conception? How is the one before the ages in time? How did the nature of the one who contained the uncontainable enter the womb? How has flesh become without being subject to change for the incorporeal? How did the divine Word, having emptied himself in the virginity, take on the form of a servant through the unspeakable, most famous in the womb? How is the perfect child? How is the one who feeds on breasts? How is the one who encompasses all within his embrace? How is the "father of the coming age" (Psalm 2:7) an infant? How is the one above and below? How is the one in the heavens and upon the earth? How is the one who drives the cherubic chariots with steeds? How is the "one in the bosom of the Father" (John 1:18) in a manger? How is the "one who drives down the leveled ones in strength" (Psalm 18:4) in a manger? And all these other things, all of which it is a terror to speak?' But after receiving gifts, they silently understood the manger, and, presenting reverence appropriate to the King and God after the question, they were followers of Christ with joy, having been revealed as the first fruits of divine knowledge to the nations.

The nations envied them; but the Jews, being unyielding, rather stiff-necked, did not hasten to imitate those led from afar by a star, even after having seen the 'sun of righteousness' (Malachi 4:2) in their own places for recognition. I, seeing your eagerness for the divine words and your loving concern for those explaining them, overcome by your love of hearing, I am stirred by the desire for teaching, delighted by the harmony of your love; for you, as many students as you are, continually gather around those speaking, you guide the helmsman as passengers, you hold the reins of the tongue with prayers. Who will be able to announce your zeal worthily? Who will explain your hatred towards the Greeks? Who will unfold your boldness towards the heretics? Who will be able to announce your hostility towards the Jews? For Jews are truly detestable among the others, always hungering and thirsting, not for anything, but for innocent blood, taking pleasure in nothing except throwing people into the …

title: Condemning the Jews
english: The prophets are being dragged and stoned, the righteous are being slaughtered with swords and divided by saws, and the hands and feet of the pious are being cut off. The defenders are being held by bloody hands, and the palms are being stained with the continuous slaughter of the righteous. Those who have come to such a level of impiety against our Savior that they dare to interrogate him openly are saying, 'We know that God spoke to Moses, but we do not know where this one is from.'

Whenever I want to flee from their abomination, they clearly oppose me, either by accusing the words of the prophets, or by insulting the syllables of the law, or by railing against the books of the revered Gospels. As now the divine pages have brought them before us, they utter shameless voices and say boldly what you have heard. They say, 'We know that God spoke to Moses, but we do not know where this one is from.' Oh, the shameless audacity! Oh, the uncovered gluttony of the robbers! Oh, the blind opposition of words!

Christ cried out to them, saying that he had played the flute for them, but they did not dance, and he had mourned for them, but they did not lament (Matthew 11:17). Who can reprove their ignorant and contentious attitude? Christ performed numerous miracles for them, healing the paralyzed, cleansing lepers, curing the afflicted, healing the demon-possessed, opening the eyes of the blind, raising the dead from their tombs, turning water into wine, and providing many other wonders, which are too numerous to mention. Despite all this, there is not even a spark of faith among them.

Let the Jewish scriptures be read and the pages unrolled. Do not accept the testimony of Peter or Paul, and reject the accounts of the evangelists. Instead, listen to Moses and what he wrote in the law. What did he write in the law?

title: Prophecies of Jesus
english: The Lord God will raise up a prophet for you from your brothers, like me; you will listen to him, as Isaiah prophesied when he declared, 'Behold, the virgin will have in her womb and will bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel' (Isaiah 7:14).

Jeremiah also cried out, proclaiming, 'This is our God, and no other will be reckoned besides him' (Jeremiah 10:6-7, 10, etc.), and furthermore, he stated that after these events, God would appear on earth and live among humans.

Zechariah signified the coming of a man whose name would be the rising sun, and Malachi announced that the sun of righteousness would rise, bringing healing in its wings, saying, 'The sun of righteousness will rise for you who fear my name, and healing will be in his wings' (Malachi 4:2).
The hemorrhaging woman, who was healed after many years, confirmed the word of God, along with others, when she touched the hem of his garment and received healing.

To understand the prophecies, one must carefully read Ezekiel and the 'man of desires', where Ezekiel says, 'This is the gate of the Lord, and the Lord will enter through it and go out, and the gate will be closed' (Ezekiel 44:2).
Daniel, on the other hand, saw a vision of one like a son of man coming on the clouds of heaven, saying, 'I saw, and behold, one like a son of man coming on the clouds of heaven' (Daniel 7:13).

Jacob, when blessing his sons, said that a ruler will not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his loins, until he comes to whom it has been reserved, and he is the expectation of the nations (Genesis 49:10).

David, inspired by the Spirit, sang that a mother, Zion, will say, and a man was born in her, and he founded her, the Most High, and that the mother was a virgin and remained after childbirth, keeping the seals of virginity which nature had placed, unbroken.
Let us consider the words of David, who proclaimed that righteousness will rise in his days, and that he will rule from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the earth (Psalm 72:8).

This prophecy was foretold by one of our teachers, and written down by one of the Savior's disciples, and the children of circumcision, who preached about him before, proclaimed these things, as did the descendants of Abraham.
Should we not rejoice to believe in these things?
We should be ashamed, for even the demons cry out and say, 'What do we have to do with you, Son of the living God?' (Matthew 8:29, Mark 1:24, Luke 4:34).
All creation, including angels, humans, and demons, should be ashamed of their confession about Lord Christ.

But if we reject the testimony of these witnesses, we should accept the testimony of the Father, who thunders from heaven, saying, 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased' (Matthew 3:17, 17:5).
Glory to him forever and ever, Amen.
